newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WHAT ODDS CHESTERFIELD-WREXHAM F.A. CUP FINAL?.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WHAT ODDS CHESTERFIELD-WREXHAM F.A. CUP FINAL?.

text.p: The most open F.A. Cup competition for more than 20 years moves another step nearer Wembley this weekend with a distinctly unfamiliar feel surrounding the fifth round.

For the first time since West Ham beat Fulham in the 1975 final, none of English soccer's Big Five are still in contention. Last year's finalists Manchester United and Liverpool -- as well as Everton and Arsenal -- were all eliminated in the fourth round, while Tottenham fell at Old Trafford at the first hurdle last month.
In the absence of those aristocrats -- at least one of whom has reached every one of the last 21 finals -- the liklihood is that two unfancied teams could yet reach the Cup Final in May.

The odds on second division Chesterfield and Wrexham meeting may be long ones -- bookmakers William Hill are offering 5,000-1 -- but the fifth round looks capable of producing a number of surprises to add to those which have peppered the cup this season.

The bookies have named Chelsea as 3-1 cup favourites and the London club go into their fifth-round tie at Leicester looking to reach the final for what would be the fifth time in their history -- although their only victory came in 1970 when they beat Leeds, now second-favourites at 5-1.

Chelsea, inspired by their Italians Gianfranco Zola -- who scored Italy's winner against England on Wednesday -- and Roberto di Matteo, produced one of the greatest comebacks seen in England for years when they overturned a 2-0 halftime deficit to beat Liverpool 4-2 in the last round. They will probably get past Leicester, although they may need a replay to do so.
Leeds play first division Portsmouth and one Leeds fan is so convinced they will win the cup, he placed a 10,000 pounds ($16,200) bet with bookmakers Ladbrokes on Friday.
Leeds, who knocked manager George Graham's old team Arsenal out in the last round, have not conceded a goal for four games and are becoming increasingly difficult to beat.
The match brings together old pals Graham and Terry Venables, who this week acquired a majority shareholding in the south coast club.

While Chelsea are being inspired by their Italians, Wimbledon are being inspired by arguably the most potent team spirit in the league which helped them knock out Manchester United in a replay last week.

They won't underestimate London neighbours Queens Park Rangers, who were relegated to the first division last season, but should be too strong for them and keep alive their prospect of reaching both the League Cup and F.A. Cup finals this season.
There's an intriguing possibility of an upset at Saltergate where Chesterfield, sixth in the second division, take on premier league strugglers Nottingham Forest.

Chesterfield last reached the fifth round 47 years ago and once beat Nottingham Forest 5-2 in the cup -- but that was in 1932. Of more immediate relevance was their shock 3-2 win at first division leaders Bolton in the last round.
That will keep Forest, who have improved considerably since Stuart Pearce took over from Frank Clark as player-manager in December, on their toes.

But Forest will be no pushovers and it would be illogical in the extreme if they went out to Chesterfield after coming from behind to beat Newcastle with two late goals in the last round. But that is what the cup is all about.

Yorkshire rivals Bradford City and Sheffield Wednesday meet on Sunday -- Bradford's reward for their upset win over Everton in the previous round. The clubs have never previously met in the cup but the odds are on Wednesday, who have lost just once in their last 17 matches, going through to the last eight.

There is one outstanding fourth-round tie to be settled between Blackburn and Coventry for the right to face Derby, while the other fifth-round matches feature first division Birmingham against West Ham's second division giant-killers Wrexham, and Manchester City against Middlesbrough, like Leicester and Wimbledon semifinalists in the League Cup.
Only two premier league matches are being played, with Derby facing West Ham and Tottenham at home to Arsenal in the North London derby.
Arsenal will be without goalkeeper David Seaman, who missed England's match against Italy with a knee injury, for three games but Tony Adams, who also missed the international, could return.

Tottenham, still heavily handicapped by long-term injuries to key players, will have to improve considerably on their recent performances to get anything out of a match which Arsenal start strong favourites to win in a bid to keep up their challenge for the title.
($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
